original_value: OpticalGamification (OG) is an information and communication technology (ICT)-based gamification-application that applies the elements of game design in a serious context of optics. Through setting for the variations in pre-service physics teachers’ (PPTs) access to the topics presented in this application, two OG application models are generated, namely: 1) serial model; designed to facilitate PPTs who study sequentially, and 2) random models; designed to facilitate PPTs who study randomly depends on their choices. This research is quasi-experimental with pretest posttest nonequivalent multiple group design involving 48 PPTs enrolled in wave and optics course, specifically on the topics of interference and diffraction. The results of this research indicate that there is no significant difference in the improvement of PPTs’ concept mastery in the serial and random group. Both of these models can be used as references in designing ICT-based gamification-applications for a more effective and efficient learning in the future.

result.paraphrase: OpticalGamification (OG) is an ICT-based gamification application that uses game-design elements in an optics-related serious context. By varying pre-service physics teachers’ (PPTs) access to the topics in this application, two OG models were created: 1) a serial model, intended for PPTs who learn sequentially, and 2) a random model, intended for PPTs who learn in a random order based on their choices. This quasi-experimental study used a pretest-posttest nonequivalent multiple-group design and involved 48 PPTs taking a wave and optics course, specifically on interference and diffraction. The findings show no significant difference in the improvement of PPTs’ concept mastery between the serial and random groups. Both models may serve as references for designing ICT-based gamification applications to support more effective and efficient learning in the future.
